description:
Second readability epic, from the architecture review of 2026-10-19 (after defk-x3a). Theme: state that one concept owns is spread across the compiler's env map, the ctx and the C text, so tests observe decisions by grepping C. Each child deepens one module at an existing seam.

Rules (settled in the review's grilling, 2026-10-19):
- Compiler tickets land serially, in the dependency order, each gated by a byte-identical `mix dump_c` against an untouched main checkout (noise: the DEFK_HEADER_HASH line and the path-hashed `/* defk:loop */` key in Defk.ReportTest.Gen.c) and a green `mix ci`. If the C is not identical, the ticket is not done.
- The tooling tickets (docs task, result record, header list) run in parallel at any time.
- The facts-scope ticket waits for defk-pvt; the Elixir-mode typing ticket is a spike and goes last.
- Every change through a PR (AGENTS.md); the owner merges.
- Vocabulary: module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality (codebase-design skill). CONTEXT.md gains "Error sink"; the "Copy analysis" entry names its scope.

Report: the review's HTML in the session scratchpad (architecture-review-20261019-1430.html); the numbers it quotes are in the children.
title: Readable compiler II: state owned by its module
